extracted.intended_audience: NSF program officers, MER co-directors, program evaluators, and academic mathematicians interested in mathematics-education reform
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation criteria and measures used to judge the effectiveness, reach, and impacts of the Mathematicians and Education Reform (MER) Forum, including individual and departmental outcomes, communications, and systemic change. The rubric is aimed at assessing a voluntary professional network's influence on mathematics education reform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Influence on participant involvement in mathematics-education reform
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the extent to which MER influenced its members' involvement in mathematics-education reform at both postsecondary and K-12 levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured by participant self-reports (survey items asking extent of involvement), examples of new activities, and attribution questions (whether involvement is attributable to MER). Use both quantitative scales and qualitative examples from open-ended responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forum role as facilitator/supporter (vs initiator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether MER primarily functions as a facilitator and supporter—'taking people where they are and facilitating their movement toward an increasingly sophisticated perspective on education'—rather than as an initiator of new ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for evidence that MER validates and supports existing work (validation, awareness, networking) rather than originating innovations. Use interviews and participant statements; recognize that being a support mechanism is an accepted success criterion (report cautions that treating initiation as required would be 'too stringent').

rubrics_metrics.name: Legitimization of educational interests within research mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether MER provided legitimization of mathematics education interests among research mathematicians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicators include participants reporting increased awareness, comfort contacting colleagues about educational matters, departmental attitude shifts toward valuing education, and presence of MER at Joint Meetings. Use survey percentages (e.g., >70% comfortable contacting colleagues) and examples of departmental curricular changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness of outreach and communication activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess effectiveness of MER's communications (workshops, newsletters, mailings, posted announcements, special sessions, word of mouth).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure which channels brought people in (e.g., word of mouth reported most effective), perceived usefulness of newsletter sections, special mailings, posted announcements, and attendance/impact of Joint Meetings activities. Use survey items about how people learned of MER and ratings of communication usefulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avenues of communication — relative impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare the relative effectiveness of communication avenues (word of mouth, newsletters, MER mailings, posted announcements, Joint Meetings special sessions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reported percentages (word of mouth cited by 34% of mathematicians, 50% of educators/teachers) and qualitative data indicating newsletters are better for retention than attraction. Consider labor intensity vs return when recommending focus shifts (e.g., capitalize on word of mouth).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special sessions and joint society activities usefulness
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate MER special sessions and banquet at AMS/MAA Joint Meetings for usefulness in learning, making contacts, and supporting educational initiatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess attendance rates and participant ratings of usefulness, and categorize benefits (learning new information, networking, finding support). Note that while useful, special sessions seldom determined attendance at the overall meeting or MER workshops.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshops: learning, networking, and pedagogical modeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess MER workshops' effectiveness in validating participants' ideas, introducing new educational practices, facilitating face-to-face interactions, and modeling reform-oriented pedagogy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use participant evaluations, workshop surveys (e.g., Baton Rouge), and open-ended feedback. Look for outcomes such as reported classroom changes, acquisition of teaching/curriculum info, and desire for more modeled pedagogy in breakout sessions. Note anti-pattern: workshops that mainly summarize known ideas without modeling reform pedagogy may be less effective for practice change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breadth and focus of MER's educational initiatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess MER's topical focus (K-12, undergraduate, graduate) and whether breadth aligns with MER goals—documented shift from K-12 toward undergraduate/K-14 and growing graduate attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze workshop topics distribution (classification into general, K-12, university, systemic), newsletter topic trends, and participant time allocation. Consider whether broadened focus facilitates cross-level dialogue (e.g., teacher preparation as bridge).

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitation of undergraduate curriculum reform (including calculus reform)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate MER's role in facilitating undergraduate curriculum reform and calculus reform among participants and departments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use participant reports of involvement (e.g., ~75% considerably/very involved in undergraduate curriculum reform; 60% in calculus reform), examples of curriculum adoptions (Harvard Calculus), and departmental curricular changes observed during site visits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for K-12 related initiatives (teacher preparation and in-service)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess MER's facilitation of K-12 curriculum reform, undergraduate pre-service teacher programs, and in-service teacher programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure percent involvement (e.g., >40% of mathematicians reported considerable involvement in K-12 curriculum reform and pre-service/in-service programs), examples of collaborations with K-12 or mathematics educators, and the extent of departmental outreach activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaboration across professional communities (building bridges)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess MER's effectiveness in forging connections between mathematicians, mathematics educators, and K-12 teachers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for evidence of interdisciplinary attendance at workshops, Advisory Board membership (e.g., NCTM figures), instances of co-authorship or joint projects, and participant perceptions that MER enabled meetings not possible elsewhere. Note barrier: MER does not yet have strong institutional ties to the mathematics education community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicators of systemic (departmental/institutional) change
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess evidence that MER contributes to systemic change beyond individual practice—changes in departmental curricula, pedagogy, institutional support, and rewards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use case study site visits, reports of curricular overhaul, new graduate courses focused on pedagogy, minority enhancement programs, and changes in departmental attitudes (e.g., >50% reporting education highly valued). Treat systemic change as difficult and look for early indicators rather than expecting wholesale culture shifts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual-level outcomes: awareness, validation, support, and teaching change
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure individual benefits attributed to MER: increased awareness of issues, validation of experiences, access to supportive colleagues, and changes in classroom teaching (cooperative learning, technology use).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use survey items reporting awareness increases (e.g., >70% aware of issues), open-ended examples of changed pedagogy, and attribution items (whether changes are directly or indirectly due to MER). Track specific pedagogical changes (cooperative learning, graphing calculators, software).

rubrics_metrics.name: Departmental Network role and departmental mission alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the newly formed Departmental Network's contribution to departmental education reform and whether participating departments' missions align with MER objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess departmental demographics, prior/current educational activities, degree of faculty involvement in reform, and workshop follow-through. Use site visit observations of four departments and examples where MER facilitated departmental-level initiatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Departmental practices: graduate education reform and minority enhancement
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate departmental efforts in graduate education reform and programs to recruit/retain underrepresented minorities and women.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for concrete program examples (graduate courses on pedagogy, minority enhancement programs), levels of faculty involvement, and evidence of changes pre-/post-MER engagement from site visits and interviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: K-12 outreach by mathematics departments
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess departmental outreach activities to K-12, including in-service work, pre-service teacher preparation, and district-level collaborations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document specific outreach programs identified during site visits and via survey responses; evaluate connectivity and sustainability of such initiatives and MER's role in facilitating them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional rewards and recognition for education reform involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether departments/institutions reward or recognize faculty involvement in mathematics education reform (tenure, promotion, awards, workload expectations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect evidence from interviews and department documents about promotion criteria, incentives, and any explicit support structures; consider this a key lever for systemic change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demographics and inclusiveness of the network
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the representativeness of MER membership (gender, race, career stage) and whether MER attracts a broad cross-section of the mathematics community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use survey demographics (e.g., 77% tenured, 27% women, ~90% white) and compare to national figures; assess perceptions of exclusivity and barriers to broader participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of participant time and role balance
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess how MER participants allocate professional time among research, teaching, education reform, service, and administration and whether this aligns with departmental expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use survey time-allocation items (hours/week, percent time perceived/actual), gender comparisons (differences in time on teaching/reform), and implications for sustaining involvement without career penalty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reach and sustainability indicators (membership, mailing list, events)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure size and sustainability of MER through indicators such as newsletter mailing list size, number/frequency of workshops (approx. two per year), advisory committee structure, and CBMS publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track longitudinal metrics: mailing list (~750), count of workshops (18 to date), newsletter frequency and perceived usefulness. Use these as proxies for network vitality and sustainability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence and methodological rigor in evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Require triangulation of data sources and sound methods in judging MER's effectiveness (surveys of entire population, site visits, participant observation, interviews, document review; coding and statistical analyses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document methods: survey to entire MER population (n=730) with response rate (~32%), four departmental site visits, participant observation at functions, and mixed qualitative/quantitative analyses. Note limitations (response bias, self-report attribution).

rubrics_metrics.name: Perception of uniqueness and duplication of services
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess participant perceptions about whether MER duplicates services provided by other organizations and what unique aspects MER offers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use survey items asking whether MER duplicates other services and open-ended follow-ups to identify MER's unique niche (validation for mathematicians, cross-disciplinary meetings, presence at Joint Meetings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant connectivity and sustained networking
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure frequency and nature of follow-up contacts among MER participants (contacting colleagues about teaching, reform, research) since workshop attendance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use survey frequency categories (never, once, 2–5 times, 6–10, >10) for contacts on personal teaching, reform issues, and research. High contact frequency indicates sustained network ties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program accessibility and cost-related attendance willingness
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess participants' likelihood of attending future MER workshops under different funding scenarios (all expenses paid vs. self-funded).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use survey yes/no items asking willingness to attend under various expense assumptions to evaluate accessibility and potential barriers due to cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendations and improvement criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Include concrete, actionable recommendations as evaluation criteria (e.g., capitalize on word of mouth, expand listserver, encourage modeling of pedagogy at workshops).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat adoption of recommended improvements as a success marker for program responsiveness. Evaluate whether MER changes communication focus, listserver strategy, and workshop formats accordingly.
